en-US.name: Duplicati 2
en-US.releaseNotes:
This release is a canary release intended to be used for testing.
Automatic updates are back
The automatic updater from earlier Duplicati versions has been re-introduced, now built for the OS and CPU specific .NET builds. When an update is available, it can be installed from the new UI.
The install is handled by a small helper executable. The running instance starts the helper and exits, and the helper verifies the signed package, installs it with the method for the system (MSI, macOS pkg or DMG, deb, rpm, AppImage or zip), removes the old version where relevant, and starts the new one. Installs that need administrator permissions are elevated as required. Docker, Synology and QNAP installs cannot be updated this way and do not show the update button.
This is the first version of the new updater, so expect rough edges. When Duplicati runs as a service with a separate TrayIcon, the TrayIcon is stopped during the update so no files are locked, but it is not started again for the user. The service itself is restarted.

Restore a disk image to an image file
A full disk backup can now be restored into a disk image file instead of a physical disk, for use with a virtual machine or other disk tools, including mounting it in the OS. The image can be written as a raw image, or as a dynamic VHD or VHDX file. With the default --diskimage-restore-image-format=auto, the format is chosen from the file extension. Raw images are created as sparse files unless --diskimage-restore-image-preallocate is set.

Enable and disable backups
Each backup now has an enabled flag. A disabled backup keeps its schedule but does not run on it. The new UI shows the state and can toggle it. This adds a column to the server database, so going back to an earlier version requires downgrading the server database with duplicati-database-tool.

Scheduler and time zones
- The scheduler documented that it used the local time zone, but used UTC unless a time zone had been chosen, which only the old UI offered. The local time zone is now the default, so schedules no longer drift by an hour across daylight saving changes. The new UI can now choose the time zone for the scheduler.
- A schedule that landed on an excluded weekday was moved a day without taking daylight saving into account.
- Legacy time zone names such as CET, EST or US/Eastern are missing on newer distributions, including Debian 13 used by the Docker image, unless tzdata-legacy is installed. CET stopped the server, and EST and MST matched unrelated zones by part of their display name, so schedules ran hours off. The legacy names are now resolved to the matching zones, and display names are only matched as whole words, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- A scheduled run that was queued while the server was paused, as it is for a while after start, still ran after its schedule was removed. It is now skipped, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- --retention-policy deleted a weekly or daily backup that started a few seconds later than the previous one. The intervals now have the same time tolerance as --keep-time, 1% of the interval and at most one hour, which --disable-time-tolerance turns off, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

Destination folders that disappear
When the destination folder disappeared after it was listed but before the first upload, for example because a USB drive was unplugged or a network share dropped, the folder was created again and the backup continued into a new, empty folder, possibly on the disk the drive was mounted on. Once the drive was back, the destination was missing the files of that backup. A folder that has been listed with files in it is no longer created again. The remote synchronization tool had the same problem, and it is fixed there as well, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

FTP and FTPS
Some FTPS servers, such as vsftpd with require_ssl_reuse and FileZilla Server 1.x, require each data connection to resume the TLS session of its control connection. The .NET TLS implementation cannot do that reliably, so transfers failed with only Status is Failed and left empty files on the server. The new --ftp-tls-implementation option (--aftp-tls-implementation for aftp) chooses the TLS implementation. With the default Auto, Duplicati switches to Bouncy Castle when the server refuses a data connection for this reason, and tries again. A failed upload now includes the server's last reply, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
The FTP backend also did not read the server's reply after a download, so a download the server reported as failed was not noticed, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

Certificate validation in reports
The XMPP report accepted any server certificate, and sent the login to servers with self-signed or expired certificates without a warning. The certificate is now validated by default. For servers with a self-signed certificate, use the new --send-xmpp-accept-any-ssl-certificate, --send-xmpp-accept-specified-ssl-hash or --send-xmpp-ignore-revocation-failure options. A setup that sends to such a server stops getting reports until one of these is set, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
The mail report had no certificate options, which caused failures where the revocation check of the mail server's certificate could not complete, as reported on several Macs. The new --send-mail-accept-any-ssl-certificate, --send-mail-accept-specified-ssl-hash and --send-mail-ignore-revocation-failure options work as the ones for the HTTP report. Without them, the certificate is validated as before, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

Restore fixes
- A restore of many small files kept a timer and a callback for every block it requested, so memory grew with the number of files, up to many GB for backups with millions of files. Memory use is now flat while files are restored, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- With --restore-with-local-blocks, an original file that was locked by another program made the restore fail. The blocks that cannot be read from the original now come from the backup, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- A restore without a local database failed asking for a repair when a backup uploaded files at the same time, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- The restore file list showed the files of every version when all-versions was set on the backup or in the server settings, so a file missing from the chosen version could be selected and was then silently left out, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- A folder link that pointed one level outside the restore folder was created, while the same link to a file was skipped, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- A restored symbolic link only got its owner back when both --restore-symlink-metadata and --restore-permissions were set. --restore-permissions alone now restores the owner, without changing the target, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- RestoredSymlinks in the restore results was always 0. It now counts the restored links, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- The recovery tool restore failed for every file after the system ran out of open files. It now closes some of the open archives and continues, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

Database and remote volume fixes
- purge-broken-files could fail on a timestamp clash after it had already removed blocks, leaving the database in a state where backup, repair and purge all failed until the database was recreated. Purged versions can now be moved to a free second before the next version, and purge-broken-files checks that every version can be rewritten before it changes anything, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- A retried dlist upload could take the name of another version, which could remove a version from the destination. The retry now skips names that are already in use, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- A compact that was stopped mid-upload left records that a later volume with the same id inherited. test then reported missing blocks, and after a recreate a restore could fail, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- A standalone compact after an operation that was stopped mid-upload failed in strict mode until a backup or repair had run. It now cleans up as a backup does, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- test failed on a block volume without blocks, which a backup can upload after purge-broken-files, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- With the USN journal or change tracking, carrying the files of the previous version over took time that grew with the square of the file count. With 20000 files, this went from 32 seconds to 0.3 seconds, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

Storage providers
- Google Workspace downloads can now resume, more back-off responses are handled, and repeated attempts have a timeout. Chat files that are documents are handled better, and Drive revisions that the admin account cannot reach are skipped.
- The Microsoft 365 Chat API was called with parameters it does not support.
- Jottacloud now waits as instructed when it is rate limited.
- The Duplicati backend now reports when the key is read-only, with better messages than "AccessDenied".
- pCloud, rclone, Storj, COS and WebDAV now return file times in UTC, and the remote synchronization compares times with their time zone in mind.
- The Minio S3 client ignored --s3-list-api-version, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- An SFTP rename was not awaited, so it could return before it was done and errors were lost, thanks @JamBalaya56562.

Platform fixes
- On QNAP, shares are now bind-mounted into the environment Duplicati runs in, so they can be backed up, and are shown in the source picker.
- On distributions with SELinux enforcing, the service installed by the rpm could not connect to anything. The executables are now labeled as binaries, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- A backup failed when another program was creating a shadow copy at the same time. The snapshot is now retried until --vss-timeout, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
- Jobs saved with --snapshot-provider=Wmic from the 2.4 stable releases warned on every run and used the Native provider. Wmic now selects the WMI provider, thanks @JamBalaya56562.
